recap.text: Pocket worlds hold inhabited places like Hump Town and the Necropolis of Anser that run before crawlers arrive. Juice Box remembers dreaming she was a teacher whose students were killed by a dragon-headed man, and Louis suggests she remembers a previous time in the dungeon. Carl kills many NPCs with a flood, knowing new worker NPCs cannot be added once a level is created.

A bush elf dragging a cart for rolled-up carpets tells Carl he was once a human crawler. He warns Carl to stay away from the city in the north because an alien ripped his brother's head off at a food stand. Signet's were-castors hurry Carl to a saferoom because showrunners push suggestions to elites that make them act out of character.

Juice Box leads Team Retribution, a faction of NPCs headquartered in Larracos. Arief tells Carl that most NPCs now know about their past lives, though some shopkeepers cannot understand and a death is forever. Under the lowering ceiling of Everly's tower, a silent ogre lies down and tells her it is not inevitable.

The bugbears of Team Free Love remember the slime mines, a submarine, and a rope city. A dying bune crawler told them it was a game, and a voice offered them a race to a real place to live. Quemada the mercenary panics in the truck and begs Emberus to end it. Finley puts her to sleep with a claw and lays her in the sink.

beats.headline: The bubbles are inhabited
beats.text: The pocket worlds are not stage sets. A bubble holds Hump Town and its dromedarians on the sand, a castle of dirigible gnomes in the air, the Necropolis of Anser underneath, and every one of them was there and running before a crawler arrived.
beats.gist: Pocket worlds are not stage sets and existed before crawlers arrived.

beats.headline: A teacher who does not remember teaching
beats.text: Juice Box takes the news of Henrik's death sadly and then, strangely, happily. She tells Donut she has been dreaming of being a school teacher, and of people who came in and had to kill all of her students because the children were spreading a disease. In it she touched one of the killers, a dragon-headed man, and she can turn into one of his kind though she has never touched one awake. Louis tells her she might be remembering her last time in the dungeon. Donut has seen this before, with Fire Brandy and Tizquick.
beats.gist: Juice Box remembers dreaming of a dragon-headed man and turns into one.

beats.headline: Only NPCs
beats.text: Carl's accounting of the flood: innocent people killed today, a lot of them, but NPCs, and none of them former crawlers, who are too valuable to waste in a city razed every season. He tells himself he has spared them a bloody conflict that would have ended in their deaths anyway. The rule Zev quotes is what gives the flood its weight: new worker NPCs cannot be added once a level is created, so a drowned shopkeeper stays drowned. A distant part of him is alarmed at the attitude.
beats.gist: Carl accounts for innocent NPCs killed in a flood, noting that drowned shopkeepers stay drowned.

beats.headline: The attendant who was a crawler
beats.text: The bush elf dragging a cart for the rolled-up carpets in the registration arena tells Carl he was a human once, a crawler, a very long time ago. Everybody working the arena was, he thinks, though sometimes it is hard to tell. He usually works at Club Vanquisher. His advice is to stay on the trail and away from the city in the north, where the aliens are. Last season one of them ripped his brother's head off at a food stand, and since the guards did not see it, they did nothing. Then he jerks as if shocked and pushes his cart away.
beats.gist: A bush elf tells Carl he was once a human crawler.

beats.headline: Signet has a writers' room
beats.text: Signet's were-castors hurry Carl back to a saferoom, and it takes him a minute to see why: the showrunners pushed Signet, and she pushed them. Elites are not nearly as autonomous as regular NPCs. The producers can send them suggestions that make them act out of character, and nobody knows how far that control goes.
beats.gist: Signet's were-castors hurry Carl to a saferoom where he learns producers control Elite NPCs via suggestions.

beats.headline: They organise
beats.text: Faction Wars has ten teams now, and one of them is the NPCs: Team Retribution, the defenders, headquartered in Larracos and led by Juice Box, whom the system made a warlord to stop her killing everybody.
beats.gist: Faction Wars has ten teams, including Team Retribution, NPCs led by warlord Juice Box in Larracos.

beats.headline: Juice Box tells them
beats.text: She came through with the Larracos flood, and now an NPC calls himself an NPC out loud for the first time.
beats.gist: Juice Box arrives with the Larracos flood and an NPC calls himself an NPC out loud.

beats.headline: An uncle among the Jatismara
beats.text: Arief mentions another season, and Carl stops in the street. Arief does not remember one; he believes he is new, like most of them. But some have the memory quickened. His uncle remembers dozens of seasons, fewer than Juice Box, and as one of the Jatismara sits on her war council. Most of the NPCs now know about their past lives. Some shopkeepers and patrons are made differently and cannot understand. For most of them, Arief believes, a death is forever.
beats.gist: Arief mentions another season, and Carl stops in the street.

beats.headline: The ogre in the sand
beats.text: Under the lowering ceiling of Everly's tower, one of her last two mercenaries, an ogre who has not said one word since she hired him, stops digging and lies down beside her. There is a flash deep in the back of his eyes, like a screen booting up. Maybe there is more to it than this, he says, as the ceiling reaches his face. Maybe it is not inevitable, like she says.
beats.gist: An ogre lies beside Everly under a lowering ceiling and says it is not inevitable.

beats.headline: Racing for a way out
beats.text: The bugbears of Team Free Love remember. They were brothers, then enemies, usually cousins: the slime mines, a submarine, a rope city, a different place each time. A dying bune crawler told them it was all a game, and something clicked. They remember the cold in between too, which they are not supposed to. Then a voice offered them a choice: go back into the cold, or race. Win fair and square and be taken to a real place to live, and never go to the in-between again. Lose, and at least it is over.
beats.gist: Team Free Love bugbears remember being brothers, enemies, and cousins in slime mines, a submarine, and rope cities.

beats.headline: A fire fairy comes apart
beats.text: Hearing it said out loud does this. Since the back room with Akuma, Quemada the mercenary has gone quiet, then sobbing, then into a full panic in the truck: didn't something break in you when you heard it, Fin? Don't you see what we are? We've been doing this over and over. She asks Emberus to speak to her and begs to end it all. Finley puts her to sleep with a claw and lays her in the sink.
beats.gist: Quemada panics in the truck and begs Emberus to end it all; Finley puts her to sleep.
